What this is. Advan's POI list is built from business polygons, so free public parks are out of universe — identical in 2019, 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025. Park visits themselves exist only in Veraset Visits (~44 GB per national day).

What is measured. Weekly Advan foot traffic to the 895 venues that fall inside a SafeGraph park boundary — museums, concessions, parking, rec centers. Each venue is attributed to the smallest containing polygon, since parks nest.

Coverage gap. Only 223 of 1,005 sizable parks contain any venue, skewed to large destination parks. Neighborhood parks are invisible here.

Suspect polygons. Mislabelled malls (Westfield Playtown), landmark POIs carrying a default 30,902 m² synthetic shape (Walk of Fame, Beverly Hills Sign, 94 others), and geocoding errors (Maluaka Beach Maui). Excluded unless toggled on.

Why 82 became 28. The first screen asked only whether a polygon looked like a park. It let Pike Park through — eight venues, six of them a parking structure and a convention centre — because SUB_CATEGORY values carry a trailing space in the source, so the exact-match filter silently missed them. The second screen lists what belongs inside a park and drops anything you book or pay to enter: golf, RV parks, theme parks, marinas. Griffith Park and Sepulveda Basin are kept by name, since municipal golf inside a large public park is park land.

Not causal. No control group, no panel-attrition correction, venue mix varies by park. Exploratory only.
